advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Join the stderr drainer thread before reading `captured` in `_fail`, so the failure message contains the complete (drained) stderr rather than a racy partial read.
evidence: `stderr = _redact_cmd(b"".join(captured).decode("utf-8", "replace").strip())` at snapshot.py:297 reads `captured` from the main thread
`drainer = threading.Thread(target=_drain, args=(proc.stderr, captured), daemon=True)` at snapshot.py:256 has the drainer thread appending to the same `captured` list
`drainer.join(timeout=_REAP_TIMEOUT)` at snapshot.py:275 only runs in the `finally` AFTER `_extract_stream` (which calls `_fail`) has completed, so `_fail`'s read races the still-running drainer
advisory.finding: The stderr-draining thread appends to the shared `captured` list concurrently with the main thread reading it (`b"".join(captured)`) inside `_fail`, which runs before `drainer.join()`. On a non-timeout failure the error message's redacted stderr can be a partial/truncated read because the drainer thread has not finished (it is only joined in the `finally` of `_stream_archive`, after `_extract_stream` has already returned/raised).
advisory.suggested_fix: Join the drainer (with a bounded timeout) at the start of `_fail`, or pass a completed bytes payload rather than the live list, before calling `b"".join(captured)`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Increment `kept` by the number of bytes actually appended (`len(chunk[: cap - kept])`), not the full chunk length.
evidence: `sink.append(chunk[: cap - kept])` at snapshot.py:228 appends at most `cap - kept` bytes
`kept += len(chunk)` at snapshot.py:229 adds the full chunk size, not the sliced length
advisory.finding: In `_drain`, the retained-bytes counter is incremented by the full chunk length (`kept += len(chunk)`) rather than by the length actually appended (`len(chunk[: cap - kept])`). The append is correctly slice-bounded so the sink never exceeds `cap`, but `kept` overcounts once a partial slice is taken, so the accounting is inaccurate.
advisory.suggested_fix: appended = chunk[: cap - kept]; sink.append(appended); kept += len(appended)

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Gate the POSIX-only snapshot-bound tests with a platform skip marker (e.g. skip on Windows) so they do not error on non-POSIX runners.
evidence: `shim.write_text(_FAKE_GIT); shim.chmod(0o755)` with a `#!/usr/bin/env python3` shebang relies on POSIX exec semantics
advisory.finding: The new test relies on POSIX-only primitives (os.killpg/os.getpgid, signal.SIGKILL, start_new_session=True, and a shebang-executable Python `git` shim), so it will fail or error on Windows rather than skip.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert the stall-abort seam is spliced ahead of the subcommand by structure (e.g. that snap.stall_abort_args() output appears before 'archive'), not by pinning another module's resolved config values 1000/10.
evidence: Test: `assert "http.lowSpeedLimit=1000" in argv, argv` / `assert "http.lowSpeedTime=10" in argv, argv`

Source seam: `stall_abort_args()` returns `["-c", f"http.lowSpeedLimit={floor}", "-c", f"http.lowSpeedTime={window}"]` where floor/window come from `config.resolve_stall_abort_limits(...)` — `git_fetch.py:204-207`

The values 1000/10 are module defaults of git_fetch, not snapshot: `_STALL_FLOOR_BYTES_PER_SEC = 1000` (git_fetch.py:182), `_STALL_WINDOW_SECONDS = 10` (git_fetch.py:183), resolved 'live per call' through the config seam per the docstring
Refactoring-violation criterion (a): changing those shared defaults preserves snapshot behavior (seam still spliced ahead of the subcommand) but breaks this assertion.
advisory.finding: test_archive_child_gets_devnull_stdin_and_the_stall_abort asserts the exact resolved stall-abort config values (http.lowSpeedLimit=1000, http.lowSpeedTime=10), which are the defaults of config.resolve_stall_abort_limits owned by a different module and resolvable live per call. snapshot.py's own contract is only that it splices stall_abort_args() ahead of the subcommand; a behavior-preserving change to the shared config defaults would break this snapshot test without any snapshot behavior change.
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace the two literal-value assertions with a structural check that the tokens returned by snap ... stall_abort_args() (or a '-c' pair) precede 'archive' in argv, so the test verifies snapshot's splicing contract rather than git_fetch's config defaults.
